articles.title: Los cuatro fichajes del Racing del último día de mercado debutan ante el Rayo
articles.standfirst: Pablo García se estrena, además, como goleador racinguista
articles.summary: Pablo García se estrena, además, como goleador racinguista
articles.body: El Racing caía derrotado ante el Rayo en un partido donde los cuatro fichajes que llegaron el último día de mercado acabaron debutando. Pablo García lo hizo de inicio ante las bajas de Andrés Martín e Iker Luque. Además el sevillano anotó un gol en su primer encuentro con el conjunto cántabro. En el segundo periodo llegó el turno de debutar a Almeida, Belocian y Aarón Martín. Estos tres futbolistas intentaron ser revulsivo por parte de José Alberto para intentar remontar aunque al final el Racing no pudo empatar el partido. Curiosamente Pablo García lleva dos goles esta temporada, uno con el Betis ante el Valencia y el otro frente al Rayo con la camiseta del Racing. José Alberto después del partido estaba 'contento con el rendimiento de los nuevos fichajes, falta que les conozcamos mejor' . Sergio Canales volvió a marcar con el Racing 16 años y 133 días después de su último tanto con la camiseta verdiblanca. El futbolista cántabro ejecutó una falta de forma magistral para batir a Cárdenas. Este tanto por desgracia para el Racing no sirvió de nada ya que el equipo cántabro acabó perdiendo. El anterior tanto de Canales con el conjunto montañés fue en 2010 frente al Villarreal en El Sardinero.

articles.title: Arranca el proyecto de Marc Carrasco para acabar con la 'pesadilla' del Madrid C
articles.standfirst: El nuevo técnico del segundo filial blanco asume una plantilla renovada, con campeones del triplete juvenil y fichajes ilusionantes, para impulsar al equipo tras dos años muy difíciles
articles.summary: El nuevo técnico del segundo filial blanco asume una plantilla renovada, con campeones del triplete juvenil y fichajes ilusionantes, para impulsar al equipo tras dos años muy difíciles
articles.body: El Real Madrid C debuta en Liga este domingo a las 11.00 horas ante el Atlético Albacete en Valdebebas. Lo hace con el objetivo de salir del 'túnel' deportivo. Tres entrenadores, dos promociones de descenso, un 'baile' de jugadores constante en busca de dar con la tecla, 23 victorias en 72 partidos... Son datos que reflejan la 'pesadilla' del Real Madrid C en las dos últimas temporadas. Desde su ascenso a Segunda Federación en 2024, el segundo filial blanco ha caminado sin rumbo por la categoría, zarandeado por las dificultades que lo han acompañado siempre en la preparación semanal (jugadores repartidos por el Castilla o el primer equipo), una planificación condicionada por los intereses de otros filiales más estratégicos y una incertidumbre constante en el once de prácticamente cada jornada, con jugadores 'apareciendo y desapareciendo' o compatibilizando el Madrid C con otros equipos. Una mala dinámica que acabó con el descenso de la temporada pasada, que no se hizo efectivo porque se hicieron con una de las dos plazas que quedaron libres en Segunda Federación por impagos de clubes. Ahora, en Valdebebas esperan que a la tercera sea la vencida y que el Madrid C compita a un mayor nivel. Ese reto lo liderará desde el banquillo Marc Carrasco, ex técnico del Reus fichado por el Madrid para asumir el nuevo proyecto del segundo filial madridista. Un plan ilusionante que viene marcado por una gran revolución. El nuevo técnico asume una plantilla renovada, con campeones del triplete juvenil y fichajes ilusionantes, para impulsar al equipo tras dos años muy difíciles. Respecto a la pasada temporada sólo siguen seis jugadores en plantilla (Álvaro González, Sotres, Álex Pérez, Manex, Castrelo y Álvaro Ginés). Los otros 19 son nuevos: 14 promocionados del brillante Juvenil A campeón de casi todo la pasada temporada y cinco fichajes, Aimar García y Rajado (procedentes del Atlético), Kalifa Camara (Las Rozas), Pablo Bellosillo (Rayo Vallecano) y Zinebi (Granada). Aparte, tendrá a su disposición a 'joyas' como Diego Lacosta, Bailón, Lezcano, Fran Santamaría, Cherif o Yeremaiah, en plantilla del Juvenil A pero en disposición de entrar en los planes de Marc Carrasco cuando se considere.

articles.title: Keelon Russell, Ryan Coleman-Williams Box Score Stats, Highlights, Draft Stock from Alabama-ECU
articles.summary: Alabama delivered an emphatic statement in its first game of the 2026 season.
articles.body:
Alabama delivered an emphatic statement in its first game of the 2026 season.

The Crimson Tide cruised past East Carolina 48-10 on Saturday at Bryant-Denny Stadium in Tuscaloosa.

Bama was a 27.5-point favorite coming in and had the spread covered by halftime, building a 38-7 lead. The final score could've been much worse if coach Kalen DeBoer had decided to keep his foot on the gas in the second half.

Watch: CFB QB's face bloodied after facemask penalty

Tide quarterback Keelon Russell lit up the Pirates' defense through the air and was the game's leading rusher.

The sophomore signal-caller isn't eligible for the NFL draft until 2028, but you can bet he's on the radar of pro evaluators.

The reviews were more mixed for wide receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams.

The junior provided a big highlight with a 58-yard grab in the second quarter.

However, fans were fixated more on the passes Coleman-Williams didn't catch. He had a bad drop on a wide-open throw midway through the first quarter and then couldn't haul in what would've been a touchdown on the first play of the second quarter.

Coleman-Williams changed his number and stopped wearing gloves in an effort to turn the page from a disappointing 2025 season. Instead, Saturday offered more of the same.

His production against ECU speaks for itself. The 6'0" pass-catcher has all of the tools necessary to be the best in college football at his position. That makes his inconsistency more frustrating.

Coleman-Williams needs to be better when far tougher tests are on the schedule.

Alabama will pivot to conference play in its next game. The Crimson Tide head to Lexington to play Kentucky on Sept. 12, with kickoff scheduled for 3:30 p.m. ET.

The Wildcats are likely to be a work in progress under first-year coach Will Stein, especially this early into the season. Bama fans will be expecting another straightforward victory.

articles.title: Josh Hoover, Charlie Becker's Final Box Score Stats, Highlights, Draft Stock After IU's Win vs. UNT
articles.summary: It's no easy task replacing the Heisman Trophy-winning Fernando Mendoza or a first-round pick like wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr., especially after the pair helped lead Indiana to a national championship during the 2025 season.
articles.body:
It's no easy task replacing the Heisman Trophy-winning Fernando Mendoza or a first-round pick like wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr., especially after the pair helped lead Indiana to a national championship during the 2025 season.

But at least on Saturday, Josh Hoover and Charlie Becker looked up for the task.

The Hoosiers smoked North Texas in the season debut, 52-16, closing out the fourth quarter with 21 unanswered points.

Watch: CFB QB's face bloodied after facemask penalty

Both Hoover and Becker were excellent. Here's a look at Hoover's Indiana debut:

Hoover made some fantastic throws on Saturday, leading Indiana's offense to an impressive first showing in their title defense:

And his top target, Becker, also stood out during his Hoosier debut. Here's a look at his stat line:

Suffice to say, folks on social media were feeling pretty good about that pair, especially Hoover playing through a bloodied face after suffering a violent facemask penalty:

As for the rest of the offense, Turbo Richard rushed 15 times for 58 yards and two scores, Grant Wilson had a 43-yard touchdown scamper and both Davion Chandler and Nick Marsh recorded touchdown receptions.

Defensively, Isaiah Jones led the way with 12 tackles, while Quan Sanks recorded an interception. It was a good start for the defending champs across the board.

articles.title: Sayin, Jeremiah Smith Impress, Box Score Stats, Highlights, Draft Stock from Ohio State-Ball State
articles.summary: The No. 1-ranked Ohio State Buckeyes opened the 2026 college football season with a 56-3 victory over the Ball State Cardinals, powered by standout performances from returning juniors Jeremiah Smith and Julian Sayin.
articles.body:
The No. 1-ranked Ohio State Buckeyes opened the 2026 college football season with a 56-3 victory over the Ball State Cardinals, powered by standout performances from returning juniors Jeremiah Smith and Julian Sayin.

For Ohio State's season opener, the Buckeyes were a considerable 50.5-point favorite over Ball State on Saturday morning, per FanDuel Sportsbook .

The quarterback-receiver duo picked up right where they left off last season, leading the Buckeyes to a College Football Playoff quarterfinals run, but looked even sharper as the upperclassmen emerged from the offseason.

Watch: CFB QB's face bloodied after facemask penalty

Sayin produced an outstanding first half, throwing three touchdown passes and adding a 3-yard rushing score of his own.

The Buckeyes scored on four-of-six possessions in the first half, punting just twice. Sayin was pulled midway through the third quarter with a hefty 42-3 lead built.

Smith caught two touchdown passes from Sayin, including a 48-yard score in the first quarter and a toe-tap reception in the endzone to close out the half and give the Buckeyes a 28-3 lead.

Ahead of the season, ESPN's Jordan Reid projected the receiver to be selected as high as No. 4 in the 2027 NFL draft, the first non-quarterback behind Dante Moore, Arch Manning and CJ Carr.

CBS Sports' Mike Renner concurs, believing Smith to be the first non-quarterback to go off the board, but could go top-three.

"Truthfully, he likely would have been the first non-quarterback drafted in each of the past two years had he been able to declare," Renner added.

Smith's draft stock has remained steady since his breakout freshman season with the Buckeyes, when he recorded 1,315 yards and 15 touchdowns, career highs in both categories, despite doing so on his fewest receptions over his two seasons.

Meanwhile, Sayin's breakout year came last season, emerging from the shadow of national championship-winning quarterback Will Howard. Sayin threw for 3,610 yards and 32 touchdowns with just eight interceptions in his first season as Ohio State's starting quarterback.

Despite his impressive sophomore showing and a fourth place Heisman Trophy finish, ESPN's Mel Kiper Jr. was not as confident in Sayin's draft stock, leaving him off his projected Day 1 selections.

For now, Kiper has Sayin in the "maybe" category, meaning he has plenty to prove this season if he wants to become a first-round pick.

Nevertheless, they both proved why they are a vital part of the No. 1 team in the country after Saturday's win over Ball State. But ... it was Ball State.

The two will be truly tested next Saturday against one of the projected top picks of the 2027 NFL draft in Arch Manning and the No. 5 Texas Longhorns on the road at DKR-Texas Memorial Stadium.

articles.title: Cody Gakpo outshines new Liverpool signing Bradley Barcola as Elliot Anderson gives his best Rodri impression - PL hits and misses
articles.summary: The Sky Sports football writers analyse Friday and Saturday's Premier League action...
articles.body:
Elliot Anderson (143) made more successful passes against Coventry than the entire Coventry team combined (139) on just his fourth Manchester City start. Rodri-like numbers.

He touched the ball 178 times. Won 100 per cent of his six ground duels. Drew three fouls. Covered more distance than any other Man City player. The list goes on.

In a game where Enzo Fernandez, on his debut, and free-scoring Erling Haaland drew the headlines, Anderson was equally eye-catching. He mopped up nearly every mess Man City got themselves into.

26 line-breaking passes and 21 passes into the final third gives an idea of just how punchy he was on the ball, too. His role is not simply to recycle possession but progress possession and he's doing it brilliantly. With Fernandez alongside, City's midfield looks refreshed and revived - and ready to rival anything the Premier League has to throw at them. Laura Hunter

Many attended Liverpool's game at Ipswich gearing up to see Bradley Barcola for the first time. But it was a player at the other end of Liverpool's transfer window debate who stole the show.

Perhaps the decision to keep hold of Cody Gakpo may be the crossroads moment that defines Andoni Iraola's first season. Liverpool held talks to sell the Dutchman to Man City, with Spurs also interested. But now Gakpo looks like Liverpool's best player.

His performance off the right wing against Nottingham Forest last week was impressive, but his outing at Ipswich was even better. This time from the opposite flank, he set up Alexander Isak twice with some very classy assists. That makes it three Isak goals set up by Gakpo in the last two games.

"Barcola is going to struggle to get a game with this version of Gakpo," said Jamie Carragher on social media at half-time of Liverpool's win at Portman Road. Liverpool's best piece of business may not be the £123m winger they signed, rather the winger they actually kept instead. Sam Blitz

There must be something in the water at Ipswich. Because their goalkeeper position appears to have become cursed.

The last time the Tractor Boys were promoted, Arijanet Muric arrived from Burnley as the man trusted to be their No.1. What followed was a season littered with costly mistakes at precisely the wrong moments.

Fast-forward to this season and Ipswich have changed the man between the sticks again, but seemingly not the script.

Kjell Scherpen was brought in from Belgian Pro League side Union Saint-Gilloise with the hope that a fresh face would provide some much-needed stability at the top level. Instead, his first-half performance against Liverpool suggested the curse may be real.

Scherpen was at fault for both of Liverpool's first-half goals, with Alexander Isak the grateful beneficiary on each occasion.

Goalkeeping errors are magnified at this level because margins are so thin. A team can spend 45 minutes competing well, executing its game plan and frustrating a superior opponent - only for one moment of indecision to undo all that work. That happened here.

Ipswich need Scherpen to settle quickly because they cannot afford to be fighting two battles: one against the opposition and another against their own goalkeeper.

But after Muric's struggles and now Scherpen's nightmare start, you could forgive Ipswich supporters for wondering whether the No.1 shirt comes with a curse attached. Lewis Jones

A first point but still no Premier League goal this season for Spurs.

They actually finished the game with the same number of shots as Nottingham Forest, three times as many touches in the opposition box and double the Expected Goals total.

But Omar Marmoush, in particular, failed to bring the cutting-edge quality in the final third, while Micky van de Ven and Dominic Solanke wasted good crosses with poor headers.

A small step forward for Roberto De Zerbi's project? Perhaps. But not the performance or result to ignite their supporters' hopes and convince them yet that, after the big summer spend, this season is going to be substantially better than the last. Peter Smith

Jacob Ramsey's 88th-minute goal ensured Newcastle remain unbeaten under Eddie Howe's successor Matthias Jaissle, but they might count themselves a little fortunate on this occasion. Bournemouth, by contrast, will wonder how they didn't win.

Jaissle has issues to address but Ramsey's impact showed his value and there was also a positive cameo from new £51m signing Matias Fernandez-Pardo, who emerged to warm applause when he came on as a second-half substitute alongside Ramsey.

The Belgian international is of course new to the Premier League. He was on the receiving end of a couple of meaty challenges to welcome him. But there were glimpses of his talent, too, including a clever drop of the shoulder to escape pressure in the box. He injected some much-needed energy and directness. Nick Wright

James McAtee is the man tasked with replacing Elliot Anderson for Nottingham Forest.

The 23-year-old is a different type of midfielder. He is more technical, more comfortable receiving the ball under pressure and has a natural ability to unlock defences. What he doesn't yet offer is Anderson's intensity without the ball.

But there are signs that McAtee is starting to look the part in the middle of the pitch.

Against Tottenham, he showed the creative quality that makes Glasner so keen to trust him in there, creating five chances for his team-mates while completing 91 per cent of his passes in the final third. He was also involved in the move which produced Forest's disallowed goal.

And the concern about his slight frame shouldn't be overstated. McAtee won six of his 11 duels and, importantly for a Glasner midfielder, showed an understanding of when to disrupt play with clever tactical fouls.

Glasner doesn't need McAtee to become Anderson. He needs him to bring something different while proving he can survive the ugly parts of central midfield.

If Glasner can unlock that side of his game, Forest may have found a very different - but potentially very effective - solution to Anderson's departure. Lewis Jones

It was 90+1 vs Man City. Then 90+1 vs Everton. And now 88 at Newcastle. Bournemouth's failure to see out the final minutes of matches has cost them five points in their first three Premier League games of the season.

The late goals conceded must be infuriating for boss Marco Rose, whose side would have been sitting top of the Premier League table going into Saturday's 3pm games had they held out in the final minutes of their matches so far this term.

They are the first team in Premier League history to score the opening goal in their first three games of a season and fail to win any of them.

It will be a particularly galling journey back to the south coast from Newcastle, given how Bournemouth dominated the first half and missed two good chances to add to their tally before the break, with James Tavernier and Evanilson off target before Harvey Barnes' stunner gave Newcastle hope.

Rose will also reflect on how his side seemingly allowed the game to fizzle out in that second half before Newcastle's smash and grab. Fine margins. Had they held on it would have looked like a perfect away performance. But Bournemouth's intensity and focus in the final minutes has seen them give up precious points again.

It's a major issue they must address if they are to make the most of excellent play in other aspects of their game. Peter Smith

Fantasy Premier League managers will have been pulling their hair out at Dominic Calvert-Lewin's first half display at Leeds. He had three golden chances to score.

The first saw him miss a one-on-one after five minutes and while the offside flag went up, replays showed it could have counted as the call was tight.

The second was a missed header in the build-up to Leeds' opener - so his blushes were spared there too. But the third was perhaps the biggest of the lot.

Having done all the hard work in rounding the goalkeeper, his tame effort allowed Lewis Dunk to clear from off the line.

He ended up with no goals from a tally of 0.83 xG. He lacked the ruthlessness to kill the game. "Dominic should have put the game to bed in the first half," said Daniel Farke.

Calvert-Lewin has endured a decent start to the season - rescuing a point against Brentford last week as well as being a consistent nuisance in the duels and bringing others into play.

But this was a reminder that the Leeds striker needs to show consistency on the scoresheet if he wants to get an England spot back, but also take his team to another level. Sam Blitz

Pascal Struijk may have been disappointed not to feature against former club Leeds but in fairness, there is absolutely no spot in the Brighton defence for him to get into.

Despite being signed to replace the outgoing Jan Paul Van Hecke, Struijk had to sit and watch the centre-back pairing of Luka Vuskovic and Lewis Dunk put in a mammoth shift against his former team.

Vuskovic scored the crucial leveller for Brighton - showing the attacking prowess he demonstrated in the Bundesliga at Hamburg last season. But Dunk was arguably player of the match, and helped keep the scoreline down.

The Brighton captain was everywhere throughout - making 12 clearances, twice as many as the next-best Seagulls player. The best of the dozen came to deny Dominic Calvert-Lewin from off the line in a goal-saving challenge.

And there's no spot for Struijk at left-back, given Olivier Boscagli's display in that role. Brighton's best chances came from his wand of a left boot - as he created five chances against Leeds - which was just as many as the entire Whites starters combined.

What do they feed defenders in Brighton? Sam Blitz

A miss for both teams with VAR at the forefront of the post-match discussions once again.

Brentford boss Keith Andrews was right to criticise the flow of the game and the control Thomas Bramall had at times but zero questions can be raised about the penalty.

A greater emphasis is being placed on players who do not look at the ball, have both hands on their opponent, make no attempt to play the ball or commit sustained holding of their opponent.

Keane Lewis-Potter did all four in plain sight of match officials and VAR.

Sunderland, meanwhile, were also left with a bitter taste in their mouths regarding officiating after it took longer than four minutes to disallow Dan Ballard's goal in the ninth minute.

"It's a shame because if you need four and a half minutes to make your decision, it means that you are hesitating," Regis Le Bris said after the game.

"So it wasn't a decision for us. It is what it is."

An enthralling game where momentum swung both ways should leave us talking about in-game management, the finish of Vitaly Janelt and Enzo Le Fee's late equaliser. Instead, it's VAR again. Patrick Rowe

One point from three games. Zero goals and just one shot on target. Key names like Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Ollie Watkins gone. Some might say this is a new mountain for Unai Emery to climb as Aston Villa boss. And what a mountain.

Let's not forget last season though. It took Villa five games to get off the mark in terms of goals in the league. They didn't win a game until the end of September. By Christmas, there were suggestions they were even in a title fight.

That's how quickly fortunes and perceptions can change in the Premier League, and Emery has shown he knows just how to overcome this very obstacle. If he couldn't he wouldn't have been celebrating his 200th game in charge of Aston Villa tonight.

Is that to say that a similar turnaround is coming. No. He did still have Premier League proven talent to help him turn things around in attack. The signing of Ibrahim Mbaye is exciting. George Hemmings has potential. Nicolas Jackson brings energy. But you'd probably back none of them to be more clinical than Watkins inside the 18-yard-box.

But Emery has time and again found a way. He even said post-match that this is the position he found himself in last season. He's reminded his players of that. So, while the table looks bleak and the lack of goals is a talking point, refrain from jumping to conclusions. Villa's boss is playing the cards he's been dealt and as Jamie Carragher and Thierry Henry have already argued, there's few better at doing so. Callum Bishop

Understandably, there were contrasting full-time emotions between the two newly appointed head coaches following Crystal Palace's come-from-behind victory at Fulham.

Both Alvaro Arbeola and Pierre Sage went into Saturday's London derby already under pressure having lost their opening two Premier League games, although the Spaniard had managed a win in the Carabao Cup.

And for large parts of the contest at Craven Cottage, it appeared as though the Fulham boss would be the one with the pressure-relieving three points to his name, until the visitors' second-half turnaround.

And so it was Sage speaking about the much-needed "petrol" the 3-2 win had given his players in his post-match press conference, as the Eagles avoided a third straight league defeat to kick off the campaign for the first time since 2017/18.

In contrast, the Cottagers boss was left to rue a series of first-half missed openings that cost his team the chance to also avoid starting the season with a trio of top-flight reverses for the only the third time in the club's history.

Ominously, though, on the previous two occasions it happened in 1951/52 and 2020/21, they were relegated. Rich Morgan

articles.title: Logan Costa vuelve a una titularidad 469 días después
articles.standfirst: El central recupera un puesto en el once por primera vez desde el 25 de mayo de 2025
articles.summary: El central recupera un puesto en el once por primera vez desde el 25 de mayo de 2025
articles.body: Ha tenido que esperar mucho, pero por fin Logan Costa ha vuelto a disfrutar de la sensación de sentirse titular. El central caboverdiano ha puesto así fin a una espera de 469 días desde la última vez que comenzó un partido oficial en el once inicial. Y lo hizo ante el Deportivo donde cubrió la baja de Juan Foyth. Hay que remontarse al 25 de mayo de 2025 para encontrar su anterior presencia en una alineación inicial. Fue ante el Sevilla, en La Cerámica, en un partido que terminó con victoria del Villarreal por 4-2 y que cerraba la temporada 25/26. Aquel día, Logan Costa completó los 90 minutos e incluso repartió una asistencia. Desde entonces, el camino del defensa no ha sido sencillo. Una grave lesión de ligamento cruzado frenó en seco su progresión y le obligó a permanecer durante meses lejos de los terrenos de juego. Una ausencia prolongada que explica la escasa presencia del central en las convocatorias y, sobre todo, en los partidos del Villarreal. Logan Costa ha vuelto a vestir de corto con el Villarreal desde aquel encuentro ante el Sevilla, pero sus apariciones han sido contadas. En lo que va de su regreso a la competición oficial, el defensa ha participado en únicamente dos encuentros de Liga, siempre saliendo desde el banquillo. Su reaparición llegó en la recta final de la pasada temporada. El central disputó 14 minutos ante el Rayo Vallecano, en Vallecas, y posteriormente sumó otros 15 minutos frente al Atlético de Madrid, en La Cerámica. De la misma forma, Logan Costa también ha tenido minutos durante este tiempo en compromisos de la selección de Cabo Verde en encuentros de preparación, aunque en el Mundial se quedó inédito y sin poder debutar.

articles.title: Aaron McLean's EFL takeaways: Leicester woe, inconsistent Millwall and resurgent Swindon
articles.summary: Leicester, Millwall, Swindon, Stoke and Burnley are among the talking points from this weekend's EFL matches.
articles.body:
Former Peterborough United and Hull City striker - and Final Score pundit - Aaron McLean gives his five takeaways following Saturday's action in the Championship, League One and League Two.

Questions are already being asked about Russell Martin after Leicester fell to a 4-0 defeat by Oxford United at the King Power Stadium. The Foxes are looking for a return to the Championship at the first time of asking after being relegated last season.

McLean: "I think that it's been difficult for Russell to come into a club that over the past couple of seasons has been on a constant decline and there's been a huge turnover of players.

"His biggest challenge is changing the environment and the mindset of the players. He's also at a club where there's huge pressure being in League One. For a club of that magnitude it's unacceptable.

"So I think it's going to probably take a little bit longer than I'm sure he would like. But at the same time I'm under no illusions, I feel that he is the right man for the job and you just hope that he's given the time to be able to turn things around."

'That's a sackable performance' - what next for Martin at Leicester?

Oxford Utd thump Leicester to heap pressure on Martin

Following a much-needed 4-0 win over high-flying Charlton at the bet365, which lifted them into mid-table, Stoke City are looking to push on after a poor start to the season.

McLean: "A brilliant result for Stoke up against Charlton who potentially could've gone top of the league today after having a great start themselves.

"I think that was a real statement of intent, the manner in which they beat them and that's back-to-back wins for them now, first against a Norwich side that I feel haven't got going yet but will do and a Charlton side who've had a good start to the season.

"I think the recruitment has been good in the summer. Ethan Galbraith was a brilliant signing for them, and hopefully they can continue to build and start to fulfil some of the promise that we've expected from them for the past few seasons."

Stoke hit four to end Charlton's unbeaten start

Alex Neil's Millwall are one of the most unpredictable clubs in the top four divisions. After five games the Lions have lost two matches and won three, including Saturday's emphatic 4-0 victory over Bolton at The Den, which also saw two late red cards.

McLean: "Millwall never seem to draw. They had a brilliant start to the season, wining their first two games then back-to-back defeats, but they're very much back on the horse today after a magnificent performance.

"I fully expect them to be in the shake up at the end of the season. I think that they are a team where it's all or nothing. They will win plenty of games and they will lose a few along the way, but I think that they've got more than enough in the squad to be competing."

Late Dykes double seals Millwall win over Bolton

Burnley still to gel under new management

Burnley sit bottom of the Championship, having been playing against the giants of English football in the Premier League less than six months ago. Their hopes of a first win of the season were squashed late on with Bristol City scoring two goals in the final 10 minutes at Turf Moor.

McLean: "They need to find some kind of cohesion and togetherness at the moment. They just look like a team that's been relegated and a team that is still suffering from the hangover of last season.

"Obviously with a new manager [Nicky Hayen], he needs to get his message across to the boys as he needs to get some kind of confidence into them, but the only way they're going to do that is by sticking together and grinding out a result.

"I think once they get their first win on the board and start to get a little bit of confidence they have got good players in their squad. I think Hayen needs to be given a bit of time. It's far too early in this season to be making decisions on a manager's future."

Bristol City hit late winner to leave Burnley bottom

Ian Holloway has got Swindon Town flying in League Two. They currently sit second behind Bristol Rovers with three wins in their past four matches, with Aaron Drinan's hat-trick securing a 3-1 home victory over Colchester on Saturday.

McLean: "I'm confident that Swindon will do really well this season. I think they'll be really disappointed that they didn't make the play-offs last year. They just missed out and hit a really bad patch of form at the wrong time.

"But I think with a striker like Aaron Drinan, who got a hat-trick today and scored 22 league goals last season, I expect him to probably get even more than that this season. And with the experience they had from last year, I expect them to be fully challenging for automatic promotion this season."

Aaron McLean was speaking to BBC Sport England's Ben Marvell.

articles.title: El Barcelona y el arte del gol
articles.standfirst: Las azulgrana ganan al Sevilla con otra exhibición ofensiva
articles.summary: Las azulgrana ganan al Sevilla con otra exhibición ofensiva
articles.body: El Barcelona saldó su visita al estadio Jesús Navas con una contundente victoria (0-4) ante el Sevilla. El equipo que dirige Pere Romeu, que alcanzó los 100 partidos en el banquillo azulgrana, volvió a utilizar la fórmula de ‘Goleada+Portería a cero=Liderato’. Las visitantes apenas tardaron nueve minutos en abrir el cerrojo local. Lo hizo en una jugada bien perfilada por el carril diestro, donde un centro de Graham se paseó por el área sevillista hasta que Brugts tocó el balón para meterlo en la jaula. A pesar de un par de tímidas reacciones en las botas de Andrea y Laura Pérez, el monólogo azulgrana fue total. Descargando el juego por la banda de Graham y teniendo opciones a balón parado en dos córners cabeceados por Paredes al tejado de la meta defendida por Sullastres. A cinco minutos para el descanso, Schertenleib estrelló un balón en el poste con un zapatazo desde la frontal que posteriormente se paseó por la línea de gol sin que llegara a entrar en ningún momento. El premio llegaría en el añadido con dos goles. El segundo partiría en la enésima arrancada de Graham por el carril diestro, alcanzando la línea de fondo y cediendo atrás para que Pina controlara, mirara donde ponerla y anotara el segundo de la noche. Después sería Torrejón quien cabeceara un córner botado por Graham y prolongado por Pajor en el primer palo. El arranque del segundo acto nada cambió. Sullastres exhibió cualidades en una triple parada en una misma jugada a disparos de Kerolin, Pajor y Vicky. Sería la madrileña quien, poco después, anotaría el cuarto al sacar provecho de la presión de Kerolin y Pajor en la salida de balón y fusilar por alto a la meta rival. Romeu pidió penalti por un agarrón de Marques sobre Pajor dentro del área, pero tras una interminable revisión en el FVS la árbitra declinó aceptar la sugerencia. El técnico aprovechó la diferencia en el marcador para dar minutos a canteranas como Lúa, Martina y Vizuete, amén de Guijarro y Kika. El Barcelona dominó hasta el pitido final e intentó, sin suerte, ampliar su renta. Tras seis de añadido, el choque llegó a su fin.

articles.title: FCS Tarleton State Upsets FBS Program for 2nd Straight Season, Beats Bowling Green
articles.summary: Division I-FCS Tarleton State defeated an FBS program for the second straight season on Saturday after taking down host Bowling Green, 20-13.
articles.body:
Division I-FCS Tarleton State defeated an FBS program for the second straight season on Saturday after taking down host Bowling Green, 20-13.

Last year, the Texans went on the road and beat Army 30-27 in double overtime.

On Saturday, Tarleton State running back Tylan Hines amassed 297 yards from scrimmage (250 rushing yards on 26 carries plus 47 receiving yards on two catches).

Quarterback Kaden Anderson also threw touchdown passes to wide receivers Tanner Schmidt (in the first quarter) and Marquis Willis (in the second) to help give the Texans a 17-0 lead. Alejandro De La Poza hit a 23-yard field goal in between those scores.

Bowling Green fought back, though. Austyn Dendy scored a touchdown on a three-yard rush late in the second quarter, and Travis Kenner hit a 40-yard field goal in the third quarter to cut the deficit to 17-10.

The two teams traded field goals early in the fourth quarter, pushing the score to 20-13.

Bowling Green had a chance late to tie or even take the lead. However, BGSU's final two drives both ended on the Tarleton State eight-yard line.

On the first occasion, Bowling Green got stuffed on a 4th-and-1.

On the second time around, the clock hit zero after Jay Kastantin hit Brennan Ridley with a 15-yard pass.

In between, Tarleton State had a 92-yard drive, thanks largely to an 83-yard Hines run, but the superstar fumbled on third down, giving BGSU one last chance following a touchback. However, Tarleton State held on for the big win.

The Texans joined Division I-FCS in 2020 after making the leap from Division II. Tarleton State is a strong program, going 12-1 last year and sharing title honors in the United Athletic Conference with Abilene Christian. They earned the No. 4 seed in the playoff bracket and reached the quarterfinals before losing to Villanova.

The 2026 Texans are 2-0 after beating Prairie View A&M 49-30 to start the season. They entered this week ranked No. 5 in the AFCA FCS Coaches poll.

articles.title: Hull City on course to avoid relegation after seven points from three matches?
articles.summary: It might be too early to settle survival talk, but newly promoted Hull City have given themselves the perfect platform to build on in the Premier League.
articles.body:
"Maybe expect to fight for a Champions League place?"

Sergej Jakirovic could not resist a joke when asked about Hull City 's remarkable start to life back in the Premier League on BBC Match of the Day.

"No, of course it is early," the head coach was quick to follow up.

Three games into a season is indeed too small a sample size to predict a club's fortunes.

But with seven points from a possible nine, three clean sheets and only two points behind early pacesetters Manchester City , the Hull supporters can be forgiven for dreaming a little.

"It's huge for our confidence coming up into the Premier League," defender John Egan told Sky Sports.

"The start is important. We got the win the first day [against Manchester United] and I think that gave everyone confidence."

If history is anything to go by, the Tigers may already have gone a long way towards securing their most important objective of the 2025-26 season - preserving their top-flight status.

No newly promoted side has been relegated after taking seven or more points from their opening three Premier League games. Looking beyond promoted sides, only three teams have gone down after doing so.

It might be far too early to settle any survival talks but, following another impressive outing in a 0-0 draw against Aston Villa on Saturday, there is no doubting Hull have given themselves the perfect platform to build on.

From League One scare to Premier League heights

As recently as last year Hull avoided relegation to League One only on goal difference.

Fast-forward 16 months and they are now going toe to toe with the big names of the Premier League.

The turnaround can be traced back to the arrival of Jakirovic before last season.

The former Bosnia international joined a club under a transfer embargo, confining them to free transfers and loans, but still made them promotion contenders.

Jakirovic guided Hull to a play-off win against a Millwall side who finished three places and 10 points above them, before Oli McBurnie's last-gasp winner against Middlesbrough secured top-flight football.

And Hull did not stay still in the summer.

They were the busiest Premier League side with 18 new signings for about £150m, with six of them, including £22m midfielder Tim Iroegbunam from Everton , arriving on deadline day.

"I know the core of my team. This is the Championship players," said Jakirovic, who signed a two-year contract extension on Friday.

"We brought the players in to put some quality there.

"The big problem for me is who didn't have a pre-season. This is a very big problem. But we will try.

"For example, on Tuesday [against Sunderland in the Carabao Cup], we will use that to give minutes, and at the end they will get a new chance."

The result? Hull have beaten Michael Carrick's United and fellow promoted side Coventry City before holding Europa League winners Villa.

Defensively, they have been outstanding.

Only Charlton in 1998-99 and Huddersfield Town in 2017-18 had kept clean sheets in each of their first three league games after promotion to the Premier League.

"The work goes into it on the training pitch," said Egan, who is part of the three-man defence, alongside Semi Ajayi and Nobel Mendy, that has yet to be breached.

"It probably started in the play-offs when we moved to that shape. We have a lot of experience and it all helps.

"We've got a lot of lads who want to work together, defend for each other, and so far, so good. We just have to keep improving."

Hull are also comfortable without possession.

No team has had less of the ball this season than Hull (29%). Since 2003-04, only West Ham in 2023-24 (27%) have had a lower figure over their first three matches.

Hull's rise is in stark contrast to last season's Championship winners Coventry, who are yet to open their account after three games.

Only one of the previous 12 promoted sides have survived after doing so - Southampton in 2012-13.

Yet Jakirovic knows Hull's work is far from done.

Wolves in 2011-12, West Brom in 2017-18 and Leeds United in 2022-23 are the three teams who were relegated despite collecting seven points from their opening three matches.

That equates to only 4% of the 78 teams to have collected seven points after three games and still go down.

It might be a low probability, but Hull do not want to take any chances.

"This is a great result for us," Jakirovic said after his side threatened to claim all three points in the closing stages against Villa at MKM Stadium.

"Seven points. Three games. Clean sheet. Let's move on.

"Our goal is to collect the points. I think around 38-40 points, so as soon as possible to get these points."

articles.title: St Mirren 1-2 Celtic: Liam Scales and Hyun-Jun Yang on target as Hoops fight back to maintain winning Premiership start
articles.summary: Report and highlights as Celtic beat St Mirren; Nikolas Agrafiotis gave the Buddies the lead from the spot after Liam Scales' handball; Camilo Duran's equaliser was ruled out; Scales levelled after the break; Yang completed the turnaround before Shim Mhueka was denied by the offside flag
articles.body:
It was the battle of the only unbeaten top-flight sides in Paisley as the Buddies looked to continue their blistering start to move top of the table, and they made the perfect start.

Nikolas Agrafiotis made no mistake from the penalty spot after Liam Scales' blatant handball as he attempted to block Chris Mochrie's effort.

The Hoops thought they had hit back when Camilo Duran knocked the ball in from Hyun Jun Yang's cross soon after, only for it to be ruled out for offside after a VAR check.

Callum McGregor, Hussain Hassan and Yang all missed chances before Scales made amends for his earlier mistake when he rose to bullet Mika Baur's corner into the net.

Duran set up Yang to calmly finish beyond keeper Jacob Chapman to complete Celtic's turnaround as they then held firm against a dogged St Mirren who had chances to level.

New signing Shim Mhueka thought he had netted his first goal in stoppage time, but he too was ruled to be offside.

It is five out of five for the champions as they move five points clear of St Mirren at the top of the table.

18: SAVE! Taylor gets a shot away from the edge of the box but Sinisalo saves.

19: PENALTY TO ST MIRREN! Mochrie's strike comes off Scales' arm, and the referee points to the spot.

22: GOAL ST MIRREN! Sinisalo went the right way, but Agrafiotis' powerful effort hits the bottom corner.

29: GOAL CELTIC! Duran with the response for Celtic!

31: NO GOAL! Celtic's celebrations are short-lived as VAR rules out Celtic's equaliser for offside.

40: SAVE! McGregor meets Baur's corner but he doesn't connect properly and Chapman keeps it out.

42: SAVE! Hassan sends in the cross, it eventually lands at Duran's feet just yards out but the Buddies keeper reacts.

48: WIDE! Hassan with a brilliant ball in for Yang, who somehow puts it past the post. What a miss!

51: GOAL CELTIC! Scales rises to head in from Baur's corner. Redemption for the defender.

55: BLOCK! St Mirren almost caught out again. Scales rises to meet another corner, but this time he heads wide.

64: BLOCK! Nygren cuts the ball back to Yang. Ramsay does well to get in front of him and send it off target.

68: GOAL CELTIC! Duran wins the ball back, Yang goes through one-on-one with Chapman and makes no mistake.

74: SAVE! Sinisalo denies Thomas as the Buddies refuse to give up.

86: CHANCE! Thomas misses from six yards. He lunges for the ball and can only stretch and put it over!

90+3: GOAL DISALLOWED! Mheuka slots home but the referee rules it out after being called to the monitor.

"Celtic were worthy winners, they deserved to win.

"They had the pressure, they had the possession, they had the chances and took them when they came.

"St Mirren stuck true to what the manager asked from the first whistle through to the last.

"They were open, they do want to take risks and build. They're not building just for the sake of building, they're trying to draw the press. If the press is already on they'll go direct.

"They kept themselves in there and it is brave because if you're that open against a team like Celtic then you can look silly but they didn't tonight.

"A very brave performance. You can see exactly what he [Craig McLeish] wants to do with his team."

"A fair result. Credit to St Mirren though, they never gave up and they were always in the game right up until the very end.

"I think when Celtic changed things and the wingers went off they lost a little bit of impetus near the end, but I thought over the piece they deserved the three points."

McLeish: Disappointment 'shows how far we've come'

St Mirren manager Craig McLeish speaking to Sky Sports:

"I think it shows how far we've come as a group and what we're doing. The boys are in there really disappointed that we've not taken a point from the game, at least.

"We know Celtic are going to carry a threat and they caused us problems at times.

"We still carried a threat ourselves. I think we've had 19 shots at goal, which is really good that we're carrying that threat throughout the game.

"The goals that we actually lose are probably disappointing from our point of view, but Celtic still have other chances and things as well.

"We have to dust ourselves down and go again. The good thing about football, there's always another game around the corner."

Celtic manager Martin O'Neill speaking to Sky Sports:

"We created some chances in the game, but I didn't feel any phenomenal fluency about us.

"We really dug it out at the end, coming from the goal behind against a team who are in really brilliant form.

"They played splendidly for quite some periods of the game, but we saw it through at the end, which was great."

On losing Hyun Jun Yang to international duty with South Korea, O'Neill added: "He'll be a major blow.

"He puts in so much work for us defensively as well, and he'll be a major blow for us now.

"This is his final game. He leaves now, and he's in sparkling form. He's had a really great start to the season. He took his goal brilliantly, and we will miss him badly."

articles.title: Man Utd can compete for major trophies says Michael Carrick
articles.summary: Manager Michael Carrick and chief executive Omar Berrada are united in their viewthat  Manchester United can be successful despite the club's relatively low summer spending.
articles.body:
Manchester United believe they can challenge for major honours despite being unable to match the spending power of their rivals.

United spent £148m on new players this summer, less than newly promoted Ipswich, the £300m-plus invested by Chelsea and Tottenham and the record £458m spent by Manchester City .

In their victory at Ipswich on Friday night, Liverpool fielded three players, Alexander Isak, Bradley Barcola and Florian Wirtz, who each cost more than £100m.

By contrast, United's most expensive signing this summer was Cameroon midfielder Carlos Baleba from Brighton in a deal that could reach £70m, still £19m short of the club-record £89m they paid for Paul Pogba a decade ago.

Head coach Michael Carrick says money in itself is not the answer to building a successful side and is adamant the club can compete.

"I certainly feel we can," he said. "The challenge is getting the right dynamics, the right balance and the right group together; getting the best players in the group to enhance the rest. Whether you need experience, or some younger players."

There has been some criticism of United's transfer approach, with the lack of a left-back to compete with Luke Shaw and no striking support for Benjamin Sesko two areas highlighted.

Carrick has rejected the notion restrictions have been placed on summer spending by United's hierarchy.

"The actual amount of money I understand can be a big thing but it doesn't always have to be the answer," he said.

United can manage debt and compete for trophies, says Berrada

Has United's debt has restricted the club's spending power?

Questions about that issue were raised at the Fans Forum at the end of June and respected finance blogger Swiss Ramble estimated in September 2025 that United had paid £852m in interest alone since the Glazer family's takeover in 2005.

The club's latest quarterly figures showed total borrowings of £1.29bn, including outstanding transfer fees.

United also took on an additional £91.92m when refinancing bonds in June and are yet to outline how they will fund a proposed new stadium expected to cost more than £2bn.

The club's full year accounts to 30 June are due out in the next few weeks and will show the latest picture after a season without any European football.

Against that backdrop, fans continue to protest against the Glazers at virtually every match. Yet chief executive Omar Berrada insists the club can remain competitive while managing its debt and stadium ambitions, arguing United's challenge is to operate sustainably while continuing to compete for major trophies.

"We have shown that with debt, we can not only [be] profitable, but more importantly, win trophies," Berrada told the club's Fans Forum on 30 July,. "And our aim is to do that again.

"Our role as management is to be able to operate competitively with a financial structure that's sustainable.

"We also aspire to build a new stadium, but we have to do it in a way that allows us to continue being competitive.

"We need to stay very disciplined and continue to take the right decisions on the pitch and put us in a position where we can do everything, where we can sustain the debt, aspire to build a new stadium and importantly, try to win as many trophies as we can."

The arrivals of Baleba, Andrey Santos from Chelsea and Youri Tielemans from Aston Villa , plus the emergence of 19-year-old forward Shea Lacey leads Carrick to conclude his squad is in a better position now than when they ended last season, when they finished third after winning 12 of his 17 games in charge.

"Being at this club, you've got to strive to win," said Carrick.

"That's where we want to be, and we want to try and get to that on a consistent level.

"I don't like to keep looking back, but they know what it's taken to put that run together. Granted, there was one competition, and we need to do that an awful lot more this season, but we have strengthened the group, so we feel good about what's possible."

Whether that optimism is justified will become clearer over the coming months, but Carrick believes United have assembled a squad capable of challenging despite spending significantly less than many of their rivals.

articles.title: Swansea City 0-0 Wrexham: Vitor Matos' side fail to go three points clear at the top of the Championship in Wales derby draw
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Swansea City and Wrexham at the Swansea.com Stadium on Saturday; Vitor Matos' side miss the chance to go three points clear at the top of the Championship in 0-0 draw
articles.body:
Chances were hard to come by on a night when the sold out signs went up at the Swansea.com Stadium and there was more graft than craft on show.

Neither goalkeeper was tested until Zan Vipotnik slid Moussa Yeo’s cross into the arms of Anthony Patterson nine minutes from time, while Kieffer Moore tested Swansea’s Lawrence Vigouroux in stoppage time.

Red Dragons boss Phil Parkinson might have felt Swansea should have been reduced to 10 by then following Ben Cabango’s lunge on Callum O’Hare.

Celebrity investors had stayed away with no sign of Swansea pair Snoop Dogg and Luka Modric or Wrexham co-owners Rob Mac and Ryan Reynolds.

The Pontarddulais Male Voice Choir were present, though, and a rousing pre-match rendition of Max Boyce's 'Hymns and Arias' lifted the crowd.

Swansea sat top of the table at kick-off with 10 points from four games and head coach Vitor Matos suggesting in his programme notes that they were building something special.

Wrexham had experienced a trickier start, but travelled in good spirits after recording a first win of the season at Millwall on Wednesday.

Both camps ignored the old adage of never changing winning teams - Swansea making three and Wrexham five - with the visitors handing a debut to O'Hare, a £6.5million deadline day signing from Sheffield United.

There was a lively start befitting of a derby with Ryan Longman leaving a calling card on Josh Key, much to the displeasure of Swansea supporters.

Swansea started the better and there were loud shouts for a penalty, at least from the home crowd, after 18 minutes.

Melker Widell played the ball into a central area and it struck the hand of Longman, but referee Elliot Bell was not interested.

Wrexham slowly settled, enjoyed greater possession and found space with raking diagonal balls.

One such pass from Callum Doyle released Danny Imray down the right and the wing-back got past Josh Tymon.

Imray's cross found O'Hare in the box but he was quickly surrounded by Swansea defenders and the opportunity was lost.

The first genuine chance came five minutes after the restart when Sam Smith nodded Ben Whiteman's pass into the path of O'Hare.

He took a good touch to create shooting space but his effort went across the face of goal.

Wrexham went close again when Josh Windass, one of four substitutes introduced after 62 minutes by Parkinson, drove into a congested penalty area and struck Max Cleworth before drifting wide.

Referee Bell was surrounded by angry Wrexham players after Cabango took out O'Hare on the touchline. But the verdict was a yellow card, not red, as Swansea took a one-point lead at the top.

Swansea's Vitor Matos speaking with Sky Sports:

“Happy with the clean sheet. Keeping clean sheets is quite important for building momentum. At the other end, of course I’m not happy because we could’ve won the game. We had the chances to do that. We knew it would be a quite physical one and our pitch didn’t help us as well. It was quite heavy so it was hard to keep the quality and speed we wanted.

On being a point clear at the top of the Championship: “It doesn’t mean a lot. There’s still a long way to go. It’s more important to keep the desire to fight for every game.

“We have a really tough trip to Southampton. If we keep that the desire then we have a good chance to compete.”

Wrexham's Phil Parkinson speaking with Sky Sports:

"We'll take the point. It was always going to be a tough game. I thought the lads stuck to the task at hand and grew in confidence, belief and quality as the game went on. In the end we probably had the best changes to win the game."

On Ben Cabango not being sent off: "A couple of things. Firstly Cabango grabs Kieffer [Moore] around the neck on the halfway line. That's a definite bookable offence that wasn't given. Then he has the challenge which is a straight red. It's a dangerous, out of control challenge. One which can really injure a player and the same referee sent off Callum Doyle against Oxford last year for a challenge that was nowhere near that level.

"I'll be interested when he reviews that challenge and see how he sees them in the cold light of day. Those challenges that are out of control and can injure players are the ones that, in my book, they're the ones that are reds."

articles.title: Super League: Proving difference between Champions and challengers - Wigan Warriors show Leeds Rhinos how it is done
articles.summary: Wigan Warriors moved into top spot in Super League and are one victory from winning the League Leaders' Shield; Leeds have held top spot for months until Round 26; The regular Super League season concludes with Round 27 from Thursday September 10 live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
However, Wigan reminded them on Friday that there is a difference between having signs of being a trophy team and consistently being one.

If there has been one criticism levelled at Arthur during his time at the Rhinos it has been that, in the big games, their star players do not step up and they falter.

Last year, they fell to St Helens in the play-offs when they were the clear favourites. Who can forget 'Left to Wright'. They went out early in the Challenge Cup to Wakefield Trinity. They were dominated by Wigan on a night when they could have got one hand on their first piece of silverware in 15 years.

Wigan now need one win, in Round 27 against Catalans, to make it two trophies out of two in 2026. Of course, Leeds are not yet mathematically out of the League Leaders' Shield race. If Wigan lose and they win in the final round, their points difference should see them over the line.

If Wigan stand firm though and extend their trophy cabinet, there is one opportunity left for the Rhinos in 2026. It would mean the Rhinos, despite being in top spot for 15 weeks in a row, would only have the Grand Final left as an opportunity to claim silverware.

To win that, they still need to win a semi-final and then the big dance.

What happened on Saturday night is simple: One is a champion team. The other is trying to become one.

It was another big occasion that Leeds Rhinos let slip and for head coach Arthur, he said they simply "let the club down" on the night.

"We are disappointed, we did not put our best foot forward tonight," Arthur said.

"It was a big occasion for the club, not through effort, but we just let ourselves down, we let the club down tonight.

"We spoke to the boys then, it's certainly not over, but we're going to have to dust ourselves off and we've got a big game next week and we need to regain some form."

Like Arthur pointed out, it is important to note that this is not a nail in the coffin for Leeds. In a month's time, we could be lauding the Yorkshire outfit for picking up their first Grand Final win since 2015.

It would be a first major trophy since they had some legendary figures gracing the field.

Scrap that - they could be picking up the League Leaders' Shield next week if Catalans do them a favour and they can get past Hull FC.

However, Wigan have shown again this year that on their day, with their best on the field, they are a sight to behold.

"I think they're too good a team to let this opportunity slip next week," Arthur added.

"They were (the team to beat) before tonight and they just showed how much of a class outfit they are. They just outplayed us."

Leeds were shown Wigan's superiority on Saturday night. They will hope next time they meet, they will finally get to show theirs.
